characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-838 variant, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness)
characters.summary: Reed Richards of Earth-838 is a genius scientist (called 'the smartest man alive' by Mordo) and member of the Illuminati with superhuman elasticity, able to stretch and distort his body to extraordinary lengths. His only MCU combat is a brief attempt to restrain the Scarlet Witch, who killed him almost instantly.
weaknesses: His elastic body was torn apart by the Scarlet Witch's Chaos Magic; elasticity gave no protection against reality-warping magic
limitations: Combat use of his elasticity is shown only once, briefly, before his death

sources.supports: Earth-838 Reed Richards: superhuman elasticity, genius intellect, stretching his arm to restrain the Scarlet Witch, and his death by Chaos Magic in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
The MCU Wiki's main Mister Fantastic page is the Earth-828 Reed Richards (Fantastic Four: First Steps era), a different version from the Earth-838 one described in this record.

feats.claim: Stretched his arm to try to restrain the Scarlet Witch after she killed Black Bolt.
feats.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
notableResults.note: She easily repelled his attack, lifted him with Chaos Magic, shredded his limbs and torso into strings and burst his head, killing him.

unknowns: Roster identity: the MCU Wiki's main Mister Fantastic page is the Earth-828 Reed Richards (Fantastic Four: First Steps), who has far more shown feats (holding back Giganto's hand, surviving being stretched by Galactus, Teleportation Bridges, Fantasticar). This record describes only the Earth-838 cameo. Owner should decide which MCU version the roster id 'mcu:Mister Fantastic' means.
Full combat limits of the Earth-838 Reed's elasticity are not shown in the MCU.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Spider-Man: Homecoming, Far From Home, No Way Home)
characters.summary: Michelle Jones-Watson (MJ) is a smart, observant high school student and ally of Peter Parker who deduced his identity on her own. She has no superhuman abilities; in combat situations she relies on improvisation, such as smashing one of Mysterio's drones with a mace from a museum display.

mechanisms: Evasion (fled from the Lizard through the Statue of Liberty)

limitations: No superpowers, combat training or specialized gear shown.

sources.supports: MCU Wiki URL that served the Michelle Jones-Watson character article when fetched: mace attack on a drone in the Tower of London museum during the Battle of London, skills (intellect, investigation), and the Liberty Island events.

feats.claim: Grabbed a mace from a Tower of London museum display case and used it to smash one of Mysterio's drones.

unknowns: No combat against a named opponent is shown; at Liberty Island she was chased by the Lizard and fell when the scaffolding collapsed, but she was not captured by the Green Goblin (he took Parker away).
Future combat training developments post-trilogy.

characters.summary: Monica Rambeau is a S.W.O.R.D. agent who gained energy powers after passing through the Westview Hex barrier. She can perceive and manipulate all wavelengths of the electromagnetic spectrum, phase through attacks, absorb and redirect energy and kinetic force, and (from The Marvels) fly.

techniques: Redirecting absorbed energy back at the attacker

mechanisms: Intangibility (phasing through gunshots and thrust weapons)
Kinetic and energy absorption (bullets, falls, Dar-Benn's Universal Weapon blast)

weaknesses: Her energy blasts can be redirected by a capable opponent (Dar-Benn did so)
limitations: While quantum-entangled with Carol Danvers and Kamala Khan, using powers at the same time swapped their positions (the entanglement ended after the Dar-Benn fight)

sources.supports: MCU Wiki URL that served the Monica Rambeau character article when fetched: powers (intangibility, absorption, energy perception, flight), the Battle of Westview, Wanda's attack, the S.W.O.R.D. agents, the entanglement, and the fight with Dar-Benn.

unknowns: Full offensive destructive capacity following events in The Marvels, after she remained on the other side of the closed rift.

characters.summary: Marc Spector is a former mercenary and the avatar of the Egyptian moon god Khonshu. In the Moon Knight suit he has superhuman strength, durability, speed, agility, reflexes and a greatly increased healing factor; he throws Crescent Blades pulled from the suit's emblem and, uniquely among the alters, can fly using his cape.

techniques: Thrown Crescent Blades (sometimes several at once)

mechanisms: Greatly increased healing factor while suited

weaknesses: Dissociative identity disorder: uncontrolled switches between alters can be exploited or cause blackouts mid-fight
mobility: Flight using his cape (Battle of Cairo)
limitations: Suit powers depend on his bond with Khonshu

characters.summary: Jake Lockley is the third, hidden alter sharing Marc Spector's body, unknown to Marc and Steven until late in the series. Spanish is his default language and he is the most ruthless of the three: he kills Ammit's disciples while the others are not in control, and Khonshu chose him as avatar to finally kill Arthur Harrow.

mechanisms: Shares the suited avatar's superhuman durability

weaknesses: Shares one body with Marc Spector and Steven Grant; control can switch between alters
mobility: Drives a limousine (license plate SPKTR); no separate mobility powers shown
limitations: Acts as Khonshu's chosen avatar, outside the knowledge of the other alters
characters.formDifferences: The third alter in control of the body: fluent in Spanish (his default language), operates without the other alters' knowledge and is willing to kill where Marc refuses (he shoots Harrow dead on Khonshu's orders). The suit can appear differently depending on which alter is in control.

sources.supports: MCU Wiki URL that served the Marc Spector (Moon Knight) character article when fetched; its sections on Jake Lockley cover his kills in Cairo, the final battle, killing Harrow, his Spanish and his limousine.

characters.summary: Mr. Knight is the form the avatar suit takes when Steven Grant is in control: a tailored white suit, with truncheons he can summon. Steven is far less effective in combat than Marc and often hands control over mid-fight, but with Khonshu's help Mr. Knight altered the night sky.
weaknesses: Lack of combat skill compared to Marc Spector; tends to cede control mid-fight
mobility: Suited superhuman agility (no flight: only Spector flies, using his cape)
limitations: Cannot fly; flight is unique to Spector's Moon Knight form
Altering the night sky required Khonshu, who was imprisoned in stone as a result
characters.formDifferences: The white three-piece-suit form of the avatar armor when Steven Grant is in control; uses summoned truncheons instead of Moon Knight's Crescent Blades, lacks Spector's cape flight, and is far less combat-effective.

characters.summary: Karl Mordo is a master of the mystic arts trained at Kamar-Taj and a highly skilled armed and unarmed martial artist. He fights with the Staff of the Living Tribunal, travels by Sling Ring portals and the Vaulting Boots of Valtorr, and after breaking with Strange he stripped Jonathan Pangborn of his magic.

techniques: Staff of the Living Tribunal (extends into a chain-like flail or whip)

weaknesses: Rigid refusal to break the natural law; this inflexibility turned him against the Ancient One and Strange
mobility: Vaulting Boots of Valtorr (high leaps, brief walking on air)
limitations: Portal travel relies on his Sling Ring

sources.supports: MCU Karl Mordo (Chiwetel Ejiofor): Sling Ring, Staff of the Living Tribunal, Vaulting Boots of Valtorr, martial arts, defeating three Nepalese thugs, his rigid personality, and stripping Pangborn's magic.
Mordo's encounters with Kaecilius' Zealots at the New York Sanctum, in the Mirror Dimension and at Hong Kong in Doctor Strange.

feats.claim: Single-handedly defeated three Nepalese thugs in Kathmandu.
Stripped Jonathan Pangborn of the magic that let him walk, drawing the energy out of his body.

notableResults.note: Fought them with Strange after they resumed their attack on the New York Sanctum; all were trapped in the Mirror Dimension, and the Ancient One pulled Strange and Mordo out of the fight.

campaignTags.claim: Master of the mystic arts trained at Kamar-Taj; uses eldritch magic.
Opens fiery Sling Ring portals for near-instant travel and to move between dimensions.
Wields the Staff of the Living Tribunal and uses the Vaulting Boots of Valtorr.

unknowns: Exact activities and power scaling following the events of Doctor Strange (the Earth-838 Mordo in Multiverse of Madness is a different version).

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Ms. Marvel, The Marvels)
characters.summary: Kamala Khan is a teenager whose family bangle activates her latent ability to draw on Noor Dimension energy. She forms solid purple hard-light constructs: shields and domes, giant fists strong enough to lift a Humvee, extended limbs, floating platforms to walk on air, and hard-light armor that enlarges parts of her body.

techniques: Extended hard-light limbs for reach and kicks

mechanisms: Hard-light armor (made her bulletproof in one fight)

weaknesses: Hard-light constructs can be shattered by force or a Stark Sonic Cannon
Vulnerable if disarmed or the bangle is taken (Dar-Benn targeted it)
mobility: Hard-light platforms to walk on air and jump (she cannot fly)
limitations: While entangled with Danvers and Rambeau, using powers caused them to swap places

sources.supports: Kamala Khan's hard-light powers, the bangle and Noor Dimension, the school battle with Damage Control, fights in The Marvels, and her limitations.

feats.claim: Formed giant hard-light fists that punched drones apart and lifted a Humvee.
Contained Kamran's crystalline blast inside a hard-light dome during the school battle.
Created a giant hard-light hand to rescue Danvers and Rambeau.

notableResults.note: Did not defeat them outright; stalled the agents at her school, contained Kamran's blast and punched a hole in the ground so he could escape. The crowd then shielded her from the agents.
Dar-Benn overpowered, pinned and tortured her to take the bangle during the attack on the Sun.
On Aladna, with her powers unusable because of the entanglement, she defeated Kree soldiers using her scarf as a whip.

conditional.dependsOn: The bangle activating her latent Noor Dimension powers (the source says the power comes from within her)

unknowns: Full potential of her genetic mutation unlocked by the bangle.
Whether the bangle counts as a magic item: the source ties it to the Noor Dimension but does not call it magic.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Spider-Man: Far From Home)
characters.summary: Quentin Beck is a former Stark Industries engineer, fired by Tony Stark, who helped develop the holographic technology Stark rebranded as B.A.R.F. He has no powers: with a crew of disgruntled ex-Stark employees, E.D.I.T.H. and a fleet of cloaked Stark combat drones carrying holographic projectors, he staged superhero battles and attacks that caused real damage.
weaknesses: No powers or hand-to-hand skill; helpless once his drones are destroyed
Illusions can be seen through by senses that do not rely on sight (Spider-Man's enhanced senses detected the invisible drones)
mobility: Standard human movement (flight was only a hologram)
limitations: Illusions and attacks depend on his drones, projectors and E.D.I.T.H. access
